title: Rate smoothing middleware and commitment mirroring
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Introduces a rate-smoothing middleware for Dedicated ingress and a lightweight commitment mirroring layer to reduce headroom churn. Improves tail latency stability under bursty traffic and surfaces per-tenant smoothing telemetry.
description: Context: Dedicated fleets have been sensitive to short microbursts that cause transient headroom allocation churn and noisy eviction signals. ENG-3742 asked for a low-risk, deployable mitigation that reduces re-provision noise without changing long-term guarantees. This PR adds two cooperating subsystems: (1) a lightweight rate-smoothing middleware in the request admission path that applies an elastic token-leaky envelope per tenant/pool to smooth instantaneous qps spikes, and (2) a commitment mirroring component that mirrors short-lived burst reservations into a transient escrow so the autoscaler sees a smoothed view of committed throughput. Design goals: preserve throughput guarantees, keep per-tenant latency targets, make smoothing configurable per customer tier, and emit clear telemetry for offline tuning. The middleware is intentionally conservative: it never drops requests (it delays or assigns to a soft-queue), it respects priority tiers, and it exposes a fast-path for requests with explicit SLO bypass tokens. The mirroring layer is best-effort and only affects the autoscaler's input signal, not billing or long-term reservations. Configuration knobs: smoothing_window_ms (default 250ms), burst_capacity_factor (default 1.5), escrow_decay_seconds (default 60), priority_bypass_labels. Rollout: feature-flagged, gated by a canary group (10% of fleet), with automatic rollback on latency or error regressions. Motivation: operator and customer telemetry showed 40-60% of autoscaler upscales that reconciled within 2 minutes were driven by sub-second QPS spikes; smoothing reduces unnecessary transient warmups and evictions, lowering churn costs and improving tail latency. Implementation notes: the middleware is placed in the dedicated-gateway request pipeline just after auth; it maintains a small token bucket per tenant keyed by tenant_id; tokens replenish at a smoothed qps estimated using an EWMA. The commitment mirroring subsystem runs inside the reservation controller; it intercepts short reservation intents (<= 90s) and writes a mirrored entry into a transient escrow ledger that the autoscaler reads as a secondary signal. Safety: mirrors are bounded, expire, and are capped per-tenant to avoid maskingly hiding real overcommit. Observability: new telemetry includes tenant.smoothing.applied_rate, tenant.smoothing.delayed_requests, escrow.active_mirrors, escrow.mirrors_expired, autoscaler.mirrored_input_ratio, and histograms for delay_ms and mirror_size_tokens. Also added alarms for mirror_fill_rate and smoothing_backpressure to detect misconfigurations. Backwards compatibility: default feature flag off for existing clusters; when enabled, behaves as explained. Rolling upgrade strategy provided in NOTES. References: ENG-3742 (linear), SUP-908 (customer incident), PM-112 (prioritization).
commits: 1) Add smoothing middleware scaffold and unit tests; 2) Implement token leaky envelope with EWMA estimator; 3) Add commitment escrow ledger and mirror writer; 4) Integrate mirrored feed into autoscaler delta-input; 5) Add metrics, dashboards, and runbooks; 6) Add e2e canary job and gating; 7) Fix race in ledger cleanup after initial review.

review_comments:
Samir Patel: Requested more detail on the EWMA half-life and a rationale for 250ms default; suggested adding an integration test that simulates 200ms bursts.
Ava Martinez (author): Added comment block explaining half-life choices (approx 300ms effective) and added synthetic burst test in mirrored_input_adapter_test.go.
Leah Chen: Asked for safety caps to ensure mirrors cannot be used to bypass per-tenant quota; requested explicit unit tests for mirror expiry.
Ava Martinez: Added mirror cap config and expiry tests; clarified in docs that mirrors are not billing-affecting.
Marco Ruiz: Noted potential latency regression for cold paths; asked to add a fast-path bypass for high-priority traffic and to add histograms for delay_ms.
Ava Martinez: Implemented priority bypass and added delay_ms histograms and alert thresholds.
CI bot: initial build failed due to a data race in ledger cleanup on Go race detector.
Ava Martinez: Fixed race by adding a short-lived mutex and reran CI.
Leah Chen: Approved after seeing e2e canary results. Samir Patel: Approved with a minor nits label. Marco Ruiz: Approved.
ci_checks: Pipeline: lint (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-smoke (pass), canary-e2e (pass on canary subset), load-test (pass within 95th-percentile SLO), race-detector (pass after fix). Flaky test: reservation/escrow/ledger_test.go had a flake on initial run; rerun passed. Canary jobs were throttled once due to an infra quota; rerun completed successfully.
merge_outcome: Merged into main via squash on 2025-10-22 by Ava Martinez. Post-merge actions: created a rollout ticket to turn the feature flag on for 10% canary group for 72 hours, scheduled a metrics review in 48 hours, and a follow-up tuning ticket (ENG-3810) for adjusting default smoothing_window_ms based on live telemetry.
notes: Operational runbook included under docs/runbooks/smoothing_canary.md. Key knobs to tune in production: smoothing_window_ms, escrow_decay_seconds, mirror_cap_per_tenant, priority_bypass_labels. If autoscaler mirrored_input_ratio > 0.8 and headroom_reclaim_rate increases, consider reducing mirror_cap or lowering smoothing_window_ms.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: conservative defaults and feature-flag reduce blast radius; main risk is masking genuine capacity pressure if mirror caps misconfigured. Added alarms and a manual rollback path.
changelog_entry: Added rate-smoothing middleware for Dedicated gateway and a commitment mirroring layer to stabilize autoscaler input and reduce transient provisioning churn. Configurable, feature-flagged, telemetry-enabled.
security_review: Not a data exfil vector; mirrors are internal-only and do not alter billing. Security reviewed by Leah Chen on 2025-10-15.
